notes: Every title is a fixed template with this project's own words substituted in, and every option carries its template, its fragments and the row, field and span each fragment was read from. No title was written by a model and none was invented.

One of the six categories is known by a name of the brief's own choosing, and that name is kept as a declared label on the category's record, beside a one-line definition of the wording pattern it means and a statement that it promises nothing. That name is a NAME and not a claim: the app's rule against claims is unchanged by it, and every sentence this plan writes is still checked against that rule.

A score is the count of an axis's five named wordings that are present in the title, so it is always the number of true verdicts on that axis — each verdict, and the measurement behind it, is carried beside the number.

The curiosity and click-potential axes count overlapping wordings of the same title from two different lists, and the clarity, emotional and topic-relevance axes share some of their wordings too. Six numbers on a title are not six independent measurements and must not be read as a profile of anything.

declaration.statement: Each of the 9 criteria the brief asks for is the count of five named tokens or wordings of that concept's own specification that are present, so each is a whole number from 0 to 5, and each record carries the five verdicts and the measurement behind each one, so the number can be checked by re-reading the specification.
declaration.specificationNotPicture: Everything counted here is a token of a specification this app wrote: a declared zone, a declared typography, stroke, palette or pairing token, or a count taken on the project's own text. No image exists, none was rendered and none is implied, so no verdict here is an observation about a picture.
declaration.whatACriterionIsNot: A criterion is a description of a specification, written by fixed rules in this app's own source file. It is not a measurement of any image, not a claim about what a viewer would notice, feel or do, not a comparison with any other thumbnail, and not a prediction of how this video would be received. No data of that kind exists in this product.
declaration.scale: 0 to 5 — the number of that criterion's five named tokens or wordings present in the concept
declaration.criteriaAreNotIndependent: Several criteria count the same declared token: the overlay's word count is counted by the curiosity, mobile-readability and minimal-text criteria, the wide margin token by the hierarchy and mobile-readability criteria, and the text zone by four of them. Nine numbers on a concept are not nine independent measurements and must not be read as a profile of anything.

background.definition: A dark field with a hard edge around the subject, so the subject's cut-out is the frame's only shape.

style.label: Heavy sans, thin outline, two tones, cut-out subject
style.definition: Heavy sans lettering with a thin outline, a palette of two tones and the subject cut out of the field.

style.label: Heavy condensed, thick outline, three tones
style.definition: Heavy condensed lettering with a thick outline and a palette of three tones, with the subject left in the field.

style.label: Slab display, no outline, two tones, cut-out subject
style.definition: Slab display lettering with no outline, a palette of two tones and the subject cut out of the field.

style.label: Body serif, thin outline, one tone
style.definition: Serif lettering with a thin outline and a single-tone palette, so the frame's own field carries the tone and the lettering stays plain.

style.label: Heavy sans, thick outline, three tones, cut-out subject
style.definition: Heavy sans lettering with a thick outline, a palette of three tones and the subject cut out of the field.

style.label: Heavy condensed, no outline, one tone
style.definition: Heavy condensed lettering with no outline and a single-tone palette, with the subject left in the field.

composition.label: Subject left, text band above
composition.definition: The subject sits in the left third and the overlay reads across a band at the top, with the wide margin reserved on every edge.

composition.label: Subject right, text band below
composition.definition: The subject sits in the right third and the overlay reads across a band at the bottom, with the wide margin reserved on every edge.

composition.label: Subject low, text in the right third
composition.definition: The subject sits in the lower third and the overlay reads down the right third, with a standard margin reserved on every edge.

composition.label: Subject centred, text band below
composition.definition: The subject sits in the centre with the overlay in a band at the bottom, and the wide margin is reserved so neither element reaches an edge.

composition.label: Subject right, text in the left third
composition.definition: The subject sits in the right third and the overlay reads down the left third, with a standard margin reserved on every edge.

composition.label: Subject left, text stacked to the right
composition.definition: The subject sits in the left third with the overlay stacked word by word in the right third, with a standard margin on every edge.

contrastPair.label: Near-white ink on the darkest declared tone
contrastPair.definition: The overlay's ink is declared as near-white and the field behind it as the concept's darkest declared tone.

contrastPair.label: Near-black ink on the lightest declared tone
contrastPair.definition: The overlay's ink is declared as near-black and the field behind it as the concept's lightest declared tone.

controls.label: Regenerate
controls.about: Advances the concept's variation position, which shifts its background, style and composition to the next entry of each of this app's fixed lists. It refuses once the ladders would cycle back to this concept's own assignment.

controls.label: Change the overlay text
controls.about: Advances the concept's overlay text to the next candidate in this project's own text ladder, and counts the words and characters of the new text again.

controls.label: Change the background
controls.about: Advances the concept's background to the next entry of this app's fixed background list, and re-declares the contrast pairing that entry's tone hint selects.

controls.label: Change the subject
controls.about: Advances the concept's dominant subject to the next candidate in this project's own subject ladder, and re-counts every criterion that rests on it.

controls.label: Change the style
controls.about: Advances the concept's style to the next entry of this app's fixed style list, and re-counts the criteria that count its typography, outline, palette and keying tokens.

controls.label: Change the composition
controls.about: Advances the concept's composition to the next entry of this app's fixed composition list, and re-counts the criteria that count its zones, its margin token and its block shape.

controls.label: Upscale
controls.about: Cannot run here. Enlarging an image needs a slot that can serve the upscaling capability, and every concept in this plan carries its image as an absence, so there is nothing to enlarge. Pressing it returns a refusal naming the capability and the environment variables the registry derives for it — it never reports that anything was enlarged.

imageAbsence.statement: No image exists for any concept in this plan: no slot serving the thumbnail_generation capability has a real call() implementation in this app, so an image is not attempted here whatever a server operator has set. Nothing was rendered, generated, fetched or substituted — and no grey box, stock photograph, placeholder or stand-in is shown in the place of one. What exists is the specification, and the specification is what this plan carries.
imageAbsence.requirement: A server operator enables it by setting the server-side env vars OPENAI_API_KEY, GOOGLE_AI_API_KEY, GOOGLE_API_KEY, REPLICATE_API_TOKEN or STABILITY_API_KEY (names only — never a value) — the same names the provider registry reads. Wiring the capability is still missing. No serving slot is wired yet, so nothing is attempted today.
imageAbsence.notSubstituted: The concepts below name a background, a style, a composition and a contrast pairing as DECLARED tokens of this app's own design vocabulary. None of them is a picture, and none of them may be read as a description of one that was produced.

records.reason: No Thumbnail row is written for any concept in this plan, so no generation status is recorded or reported for one. A row would describe an image at an Asset row, and no image was produced. This app will not write a progress status (PENDING, QUEUED, RUNNING) for work that is not happening, and will not write SUCCEEDED for an outcome no provider gave.

state.reason: The app's own AI orchestrator was asked for the thumbnail_generation capability and its answer was not_connected: it could not reach a provider for it, so no request was attempted and no model-authored concept exists. Nothing was simulated — this state is what that call returned, and the environment variable names below are the ones the app's provider registry derives for the capability.
requires: a provider wired and keyed for the thumbnail_generation capability
state.note: The app's own AI orchestrator was asked, and its own answer is recorded on this plan as it came back.

modelPath.orchestratorMessage: Provider Not Connected: no provider is configured and wired for capability "thumbnail_generation". Set one of the required server-side env vars (names only): OPENAI_API_KEY, GOOGLE_AI_API_KEY, GOOGLE_API_KEY, REPLICATE_API_TOKEN, STABILITY_API_KEY.
modelPath.authoredByModel: No concept in this package was written by a model. Every concept above was produced by this app's own rules from this project's own rows.
modelPath.note: Every concept above is rule-derived. The model-backed path is gated: it names the provider environment variables it would need and states that no model answered, rather than printing a concept list that looks generated.

notes: Every concept here is a SPECIFICATION produced by this app's own rules from this project's own rows. No image exists for any of them, none was rendered or substituted, and the image slot on each concept says so and names the provider it would need.

Several criteria count the same declared token: the overlay's word count is counted by the curiosity, mobile-readability and minimal-text criteria, the wide margin token by the hierarchy and mobile-readability criteria, and the text zone by four of them. Nine numbers on a concept are not nine independent measurements and must not be read as a profile of anything.

The concepts' overlay texts and subjects come from one ladder of this project's own stored phrases (15 overlay candidate(s), 16 subject candidate(s)), so where a project offers fewer phrases than the plan has concepts, more than one concept reuses the same overlay text or subject, and the ladder positions on each concept say exactly which.

The background, style and composition of a concept are entries of fixed lists in this app's own source file, taken by the concept's own ladder position. They are this app's own design vocabulary, not observations about a picture.

1 candidate(s) from this project's own text were dropped as overlay texts because they are longer than the 8-word bound. They were dropped, not shortened: shortening would be this app editing the project's words.

areas.label: Export job state

score.note: Computed from the 6 measured check(s) only: 30 (weight of the 5 passing check(s)) ÷ 36 (weight of the 6 measured check(s)) × 100 = 83. The 1 failing check(s) contribute 0 to the numerator.

score.basis: This score is over the 6 of 17 checks that were actually measured — 36 of the 100 declared weight. The other 11 check(s) were not measured, and this score says nothing about them: they are not counted as passes.
score.notAPrediction: This number is arithmetic over the checks that ran. It is not a prediction of how the video will perform, it is not a judgement of whether the video is worth watching, and it is not a claim that any unmeasured check passed.
score.arithmetic: 30 (weight of the 5 passing check(s)) ÷ 36 (weight of the 6 measured check(s)) × 100 = 83. The 1 failing check(s) contribute 0 to the numerator.

declaration.statement: Every check below reports one of three states: pass, fail, or not measured. A check that was not measured names the input that is missing and is never counted as a pass. The measurement sentence on each check names the input it read, the value it computed, the threshold, and where that threshold comes from.
declaration.notAPrediction: The score below is arithmetic over the checks that were measured. It is not a prediction of how the video will perform, it is not a judgement of whether the video is good, and it is not a claim that the checks that were not measured would have passed.
declaration.notAHealthJudgement: Not every requested check has an input on this project today. The ones that do not are reported as not measured, with the missing input named, rather than being dropped from the list or reported as fine.
declaration.measuredOnly: A check is measured only from a stored row, a stored cue's timecodes, a produced file's own reported stream facts, or a declared export preset's own numbers. Nothing here is estimated, sampled or assumed.

notes: No declared delivery target could be resolved, because no export job on this project declares a resolution that matches an export preset. The checks that compare a measurement with a declared target say so instead of choosing one.

The seven file checks read a produced file. No export has ever completed on this server, so the honest state of those checks is that there is no file to read — which is what they report, in the words of the missing input.
The declared weights sum to 100 and are stated per check; the score divides by the weight of the MEASURED checks only.

areas.label: Copyright
areas.question: Does this project reproduce someone else's text, lyrics, footage, image or audio, and does the licence record cover the assets it uses?
areas.reads: The project's title and description, the script's title and logline, every chapter's title and summary, every scene's title and narration, every asset's name — plus the licence rows of the project's own assets.

probes.label: A quotation of twenty characters or more
Rights or copyright language
probes.pattern: \b(?:copyright|copyrighted|all rights reserved|used with permission|courtesy of|excerpt from|reprinted from|fair use|licensed under|adapted from|based on the book|based on the novel|lyrics)\b

charactersRead.note: The number of characters in the fields this rule reads on this project. Counted from the rows at build time; an empty project reads nothing and the rule reports that.

matched.note: Characters 21–22 of asset.name on row p7a_fix_asset_no_licence.

whyItFired.value: The project's own text carries characters that read as a quotation or as a statement about rights. This app cannot tell whether the quoted characters are the project author's own words or someone else's. The pattern that matched is "A copyright symbol".

humanMustCheck.value: Check whether these characters are someone else's work, whether any exception or licence covers their use, and whether the video credits them the way the licence requires. The pattern that matched is "A copyright symbol".

flags.probeLabel: An asset with no licence row

matched.note: This flag is raised from the asset's own row id, not from the project's text: the asset has no licence record to quote.

whyItFired.value: Asset row p7a_fix_asset_no_licence has no LicensingMetadata row, so the licence that covers it is unknown and unverified. This app does not treat a missing record as permission.

humanMustCheck.value: Find the licence that covers this asset before it is published, and record it on the asset's licence row. A stock provider's own licence page is the place to read the terms; this app cannot read it.

flags.probeLabel: Attribution required by the licence row but absent from the description

matched.note: Named by asset row id; the attribution characters themselves are shown on the licence report above.

whyItFired.value: The licence row for asset p7a_fix_asset_stock stores an attribution string, and this app's own description for the project does not contain it. Whether the licence requires the credit on screen, in the description, or in both places is written in the licence, which this app cannot read.

humanMustCheck.value: Read the licence and place the credit where it requires: the description, the video, or both. Copy the attribution text from the licence report above, character for character.

capability.requirement: Examining audio, footage and image similarity needs a capability this app does not have: its registry (src/lib/ai/types.ts AI_CAPABILITIES, twenty-one entries) holds no content-moderation or matching capability, so there is no server-side env var to name and setting one would change nothing. What would be needed is the capability itself, wired to a provider — a build, not a key.
cannotDetermine: Whether the project's audio or its footage reproduces something protected — no audio fingerprinting or footage matching is wired.
Whether a quoted passage is a permitted quotation, an exception, or a reproduction that needs a licence.
Whether the assets it holds were uploaded by someone entitled to license them.

areas.humanMustCheckWhenQuiet: Read the finished video and its audio anyway: text cannot show footage, music or still images that may sit inside an asset this app never opened.

screening.statement: These are screening flags raised by named rules over this project's own rows. Each flag names the row, the field and the character span it read, quotes the characters it matched, and says what a person has to check. They are not legal clearance: this app has not cleared this video, or any part of it, for publication, and nothing here states that the video is lawful to publish.
screening.notAPass: A rule that found nothing matching it says exactly that: its own pattern list did not match this project's text. That is not a pass, not a clearance and not evidence that the area is free of risk — it reports that the rule had nothing to show.
screening.notScreenedStatement: Not screened — no capability: this app has no way to examine the part of the area that needs one, so it reports that instead of reporting a result. Nothing about those parts of the area is known here.
licenceLimits: A licence row records what this app stored about an asset. It is not a copy of the licence, it carries no terms text, and this app cannot read the licence a provider publishes today.
An asset with no licence row is unknown and unverified: this app never treats a missing record as permission.
A licence row says nothing about whether the asset is the licensor's to license, whether the upload was authorised, or whether a model was trained on material that could not be licensed.
notes: 1 asset(s) on this project have no licence row. They are raised as copyright flags from their own rows, because the app holds no licence to quote.
1 asset(s) have a licence row stating that attribution is required, and this app's own description does not contain their attribution text.
Every area reports its own rule's result AND the part of the area no capability in this app examines. Read both: the second one is why a quiet rule is not a pass.

honesty.statement: Every value in this package is either derived from this project's own rows — with the rule and the source row named on the value — or deliberately empty and saying which input is missing. No value was written by a language model, and none was invented to fill a gap. There is no search-volume, difficulty, competition, trend or estimated-traffic data anywhere in this product, and no such value exists in this package.

absentData.statement: This product has no source of search-volume, keyword-difficulty, competition, trend or estimated-traffic data, for these keywords or any others. The only numbers on a keyword are counts of its occurrences in this project's own stored text and the stated source weights of those occurrences. Nothing here may be read as a market metric, a prediction, or a promise about how anything will be received.

note: Built from this project's own rows by deterministic rules and saved as an append-only version. Every value carries its rule and source, or says which input is missing. The app's own AI orchestrator was asked once, for the seo_generation capability behind the model-backed title path, and its answer is recorded on the package — read `package.titles.modelPath` for exactly what it said. No title in this package is attributed to a model unless a provider really returned one. The thumbnail concepts are specifications, not images: read `package.thumbnails.imageAbsence` for what no image provider on this server can produce, `package.thumbnails.records` for the row this app refuses to write, and `package.thumbnails.modelPath` for what the thumbnail_generation capability itself answered.
